Sygehusmedicinregisteret (SMR) is a Danish database that tracks dispensed hospital medicine. It is of significant operational interest to DANIBD, the national clinical registry for inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). According to reports from 2023 and 2024, DANIBD is actively awaiting the technical ability to automatically extract medical treatment information from the SMR [^src1] [^src2]. 

The primary significance of this pending integration is the elimination of duplicate administrative work. Without an automated data pull from the SMR, clinics are forced to double-register medical treatments in the [[landspatientregisteret|Landspatientregisteret]] (LPR) [^src1] [^src2]. The need for better data integration from the SMR and local laboratory systems is highlighted as a crucial component in the broader national effort to maintain evidence-based, registry-driven quality monitoring for IBD patients in Denmark [^src2]. Despite methodological updates and the implementation of new treatment codes in the LPR, the automated linkage to the SMR remains an unfulfilled operational goal as of the 2024 reporting period [^src1].
